competitor_mentions.quote: a colleague had been pointing to Dashlume as an alternative that does this out of the box, but the shared template option you added recently covers what we needed

narrative: Light, infrequent contact spread over seven months with no anger anywhere in the record. A competitor (Dashlume) came up only in passing, via a colleague, and the same ticket immediately notes the newly-shipped template-sharing feature already covers the need. The seat renewal timing question from December was never explicitly answered but was never chased either - low stakes.

Same faults - dashboards, API, and alerts - recur every few months from May 2024 through mid-2025 despite each ticket being closed within a day or two, and the customer says so directly: "Whatever was fixed didn't hold" and "This is becoming a pattern rather than an incident." Individual response times look fine, but the underlying reliability problem is never actually fixed, and multiple team members (Anna, Maja) are independently reporting the same recurring breaks. Treat this as a chronic reliability account, not a well-served one.

Only six tickets in six months, but the Salesforce connector fails three separate times (auth error in December, six-hour sync delays in March, silent pause in June) and is never durably fixed. The tone stays calm and even downgrades its own urgency ("Not urgent, but would like it looked at"), which is the quiet-erosion pattern rather than reassurance - low volume with a recurring unfixed fault is a warning sign, not evidence of health.

Steady, technically detailed ticket flow across connectors, exports, and API with no anger anywhere. A scheduled export failure reported in July 2025 remains open with no confirming fix. A 5,000-record pagination cap surfaced independently on both the connector (April) and the API (September) within the same year, which reads as a genuine product limitation rather than a one-off bug, though the customer notes each calmly rather than as a complaint.

Sparse, polite traffic over thirteen months - seat reallocation, export format, alert limits, renewal reconciliation - all handled without friction. One dashboard filter-persistence complaint from November 2024 was marked unresolved and never followed up by either side, but it reads as a minor UX request rather than something actively bothering the customer. No sign of disengagement.
Just two routine tickets in one month, both resolved within days with neutral, factual tone. Nothing here suggests risk in either direction - a quiet, unremarkable account.
A single ticket - an alert rule that didn't fire - resolved in two days. Too little history to read a trend, but nothing in the text signals concern.

Four tickets in two months, three closed cleanly. An SSO redirect loop is still locking three finance-group users out of login as of the most recent related mention, with the customer noting their own IT has already ruled out anything on their end - this is a working-login blocker, not a feature gap, and is worth chasing even though the tone stays calm.

The accounting-system connector keeps disconnecting despite being marked resolved in December, and a seat billing correction from earlier in the year is still open in June. The customer's own words describe the outcome directly: "half our finance team just does month-end in Excel now and skips the platform entirely." This is not a hypothetical risk - workaround adoption for the core finance workflow is already in effect and stated plainly, the exact quiet-abandonment pattern worth flagging over louder but resolved complaints.

An API timeout recurring three times over three months ("would like an actual root cause this time rather than a retry suggestion") was eventually resolved. A report-builder freeze on large datasets went unfixed for seven months, during which the customer simply avoided building large reports rather than keep reporting it - the March 2025 ticket shows a fix, but the extended avoidance period is scar tissue worth confirming is actually gone, not just quiet.

Five minor, distinct issues over six months - bulk import, file naming, an archive gap, a duplicated alert rule, a seat removal delay - each resolved without complaint and explicitly framed as low-urgency ("not urgent, just noting"). A healthy, engaged account with no recurring faults.
One ticket, a straightforward default-role configuration question, resolved in four days. No signal of risk either way.

Five distinct, unrelated technical issues over seven months - API docs, token format, role changes, invite delay, export button - each resolved in a few days with calm, factual tone and no recurrence of any single fault. Ordinary, low-risk technical support relationship.

Only three tickets, but the dashboard filter-sharing bug reported in May was marked resolved and then confirmed broken again in July: "the fix from a couple of months ago doesn't seem to have taken hold." Anna has settled into an Excel-export workaround and explicitly downgraded the issue's priority - "there's no need to treat this as pressing" - which is the quiet-erosion pattern almost verbatim: low volume, meticulous, workaround normalised, asks shrinking.
A single, businesslike access-groups planning question ahead of a Q4 restructure, resolved in two days. Reads as routine engagement, not risk.

A steady stream of feature requests and small asks over ten months, explicitly framed with praise throughout ("Loving the platform otherwise"), culminating in two unprompted positive tickets in August and October 2025 confirming shipped improvements: "dashboard load times have improved a lot" and the new report-builder grouping is "exactly what we asked for." The one open item is a low-priority commenting feature request, not a complaint. Engaged and trending positive.

Three unrelated tickets over four months, the first two resolved without issue. The most recent ticket - a dashboard blank-page bug on mobile - remains open with no follow-up confirming a fix, which is worth a proactive check since it's both the newest and the last word from this account.

An 80-user enterprise rollout hit trouble almost immediately - three of five data connectors failed authentication at setup and were never confirmed fixed, and dashboard rendering was inconsistent across office locations from early on. By May the incidents turned serious: report builder completely down, the export queue seizing up twice in one week, and API failures on roughly 30% of calls, prompting the IT Manager to state outright, "the business case for staying on this platform becomes very hard to defend internally," and demand escalation to engineering. The most recent ticket (July) reports unresolved performance degradation hitting at least 15 users, with no indication the trend has reversed.

Eighteen tickets across fourteen months show the same faults - API errors, silent alerts, blank dashboard tiles, admin panel timeouts - cycling back every few months despite each being closed within a day or two: "Same API problem as last October... whatever the fix was clearly didn't stick." Fatigue and value complaints surface directly ("Getting tired of reporting the same thing"; "not acceptable for what we pay"). High engagement suggests they haven't given up, but the reliability pattern shows no improvement through October 2025 and deserves a structural fix, not another quick patch.

Nineteen tickets over twenty months show connectors, alerts, and exports each failing on a cycle the customer names explicitly - "keeps happening every couple of months, always the same one" for the connector, "Same export problem as February. We keep hitting the same wall" for exports, "Third time this year reporting silent alerts." No manager escalation and tone stays largely factual, but the chronic, unresolved recurrence with no improvement through the final October 2025 ticket is a real reliability risk that outward calm is masking.
